PullRequest.Title: Mermaid: share webview chunks between the Markdown preview, notebook and Markdown editor
PullRequest.Body:

Part of #349688

## What changed

`mermaid-markdown-features` built its Markdown preview, notebook renderer and Markdown editor webviews in three separate esbuild runs, each into its own folder. All three use `splitting: true`, but each run wrote its own copy of every chunk, so 204 files were byte-identical copies of others, including the `logos` and `mdi` icon packs three times over.

This PR builds the three in one esbuild run into one folder, `webview-out`, so each chunk is written once.

- `esbuild.webview.mts` makes one `run()` call with three entry points instead of three `run()` calls. The build options are unchanged (`mermaidMarkdownBuildOptions`).
- The entry modules are named after their old folders and stay at the root of `webview-out`, next to the chunks:

  | Before | After |
  |---|---|
  | `markdown-preview-out/index.js` | `webview-out/markdown-preview.js` |
  | `notebook-out/index.js` | `webview-out/notebook.js` |
  | `markdown-editor-out/index.js` | `webview-out/markdown-editor.js` |

  They can't all stay `index.js` in one folder, and they can't move into subfolders: a notebook only lets a renderer load files from the folder of its entry module (`dirname(x.entrypoint.path)` in `backLayerWebView.ts`), so chunks in a parent folder would be blocked.
- The references to the folders and entry files are updated: `package.json` (`markdown.previewScripts` and the notebook renderer entrypoint), the Markdown editor's base URI and page script (`mermaidCodeBlockEditorProvider.ts`, `editorHtml.ts`), the route in `scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`, and the exclusions in `build/filters.ts` and `.eslint-ignore`.

The entry modules load their chunks by relative URL, as before, so only the resource roots depend on the folder. The Markdown preview and the Markdown editor allow the whole extension folder, and the notebook allows the folder of the renderer's entry module, which is now `webview-out`. The content security policies don't depend on the folder.

The chat webview build (`chat-webview-out`) is unchanged. It doesn't use splitting, so its `index.js` and `index-editor.js` each contain all of Mermaid. Moving it into the same build needs its webview loading and CSP checked first, so I've left it as a follow-up for @hediet.

## Sizes

Clean builds of `main` (611b35ef942) and this branch on macOS, measured by hashing every file of the webview output folders:

| | Files | Size | Compressed file by file | Byte-identical copies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 346 | 64.8 MB | 19.7 MB | 204 files, 35.4 MB |
| After | 122 | 28.6 MB | 8.6 MB | none |

Before: `markdown-preview-out`, `notebook-out` and `markdown-editor-out` 18.2 MB each, `chat-webview-out` 10.2 MB. After: `webview-out` 18.4 MB, and `chat-webview-out` 10.2 MB, byte for byte the same as before.

Each webview loads the same code as before. Following the imports of each entry module:

| Webview | Before: up front / with lazy chunks | After: up front / with lazy chunks |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown preview | 865 KB / 18,641 KB | 866 KB / 18,641 KB |
| Notebook | 867 KB / 18,642 KB | 868 KB / 18,643 KB |
| Markdown editor | 873 KB / 18,648 KB | 873 KB / 18,649 KB |

## Validation

- `pnpm run oxlint build/filters.ts extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/esbuild.webview.mts extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/src/markdownEditor/editorHtml.ts extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/src/markdownEditor/mermaidCodeBlockEditorProvider.ts`: passed.
- `node node_modules/@typescript/native/lib/tsc.js --noEmit --project` with `extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/tsconfig.json` and with `extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/preview-src/tsconfig.json`: passed.
- `node node_modules/@typescript/native/lib/tsc.js --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck --target es2024 --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --allowImportingTsExtensions --types node --lib es2024,dom,dom.iterable extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/esbuild.webview.mts extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts`, since no project includes these two scripts: passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck` in `build/` (for `build/filters.ts`): passed.
- `node --test scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts` in `extensions/mermaid-markdown-features`: 2 passed.
- `pnpm run build-webview`, and `node extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/esbuild.webview.mts --outputRoot <folder>` as the product build runs it: both write `chat-webview-out` and `webview-out`.
- The pre-commit hygiene check: passed.
- In Code OSS built from this branch, the Markdown preview, a notebook's Markdown cells and the Markdown editor's Mermaid code blocks each rendered a flowchart, an `architecture-beta` diagram with `logos:` and `mdi:` icons, a ZenUML diagram and a flowchart with `layout: elk`, without render or console errors. Each webview loaded its files only from `webview-out`, including the lazily loaded `logos`, `mdi`, `zenuml-definition` and `elk` chunks.

## How to check that nothing else changed

- The diff only changes the build script and the places that name the output folders or entry files. `git grep -E "markdown-preview-out|mermaid-markdown-features/(notebook-out|markdown-editor-out)"` finds nothing.
- In the build script, only `entryPoints` and `outdir` change. The options are the same.
- In `extensions/mermaid-markdown-features`, after deleting the output folders, `pnpm run build-webview` writes only `chat-webview-out` and `webview-out`, and `find chat-webview-out webview-out -type f -exec shasum {} + | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -d` prints no duplicates. esbuild doesn't empty its output folder, so a second build can leave chunks of the first one behind.
- Open a Markdown file with Mermaid blocks in the Markdown preview and in the Markdown editor (Reopen Editor With… > Markdown Editor), and a notebook with a Mermaid block in a Markdown cell.

After pulling this, the old `markdown-preview-out`, `notebook-out` and `markdown-editor-out` folders are no longer ignored by git and can be deleted.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: An extra independent esbuild run traversed and bundled the same Mermaid dependency graph and emitted its own shared/lazy chunks. With the common previewSrcDir watch subscription, every source change triggered that additional fresh whole-graph build and output writes.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Redundant full Mermaid bundling and duplicate dependency-chunk writes in extension/product builds and on each debounced webview source change; static call-path evidence, not measured timings.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The editor entry is now part of the same three-entry splitting-enabled build as preview and notebook, so their common dependencies are bundled/emitted once and one subscription rebuilds the graph for a preview-source edit, rather than a third independent whole-graph build.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base line 83 started an additional standalone Markdown-editor run with splitting enabled, after standalone preview and notebook runs. All three entries import mermaid and ../shared; shared/index.ts imports the layout/ZenUML packages and iconPackConfig.ts contains the same lazy icon imports. runBuild calls esbuild.build separately for each run. In watch mode all three subscribed to the same previewSrcDir, and watchWithParcel explicitly starts an entire fresh build on every debounced change instead of retaining an esbuild context. The new lines 63-72 build these three entries in one splitting-enabled run, removing the additional duplicate dependency traversal and output emission. build/lib/extensions.ts:748-760 invokes this script in both product builds and watch mode; package.json invokes it for extension compilation and prepublish. Blame of the extra standalone editor run identifies f6d4809eda8172f8c30f13189df4eecec710130d.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compile/package the Mermaid extension or build/watch VS Code extension media
Scenarios.CriticalPath: package.json compile/prepublish waits for build-webview; build/lib/extensions.ts buildExtensionMedia waits for the script subprocess and separate type checking. Each build awaits Promise.all of the chat build and the newly combined preview/notebook/editor build. Watch changes are debounced 100 ms before fresh builds; output emission must finish before new bundles are usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the webview build script once and submit builds to the shared esbuild service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One script process for this extension before and after; Mermaid-related top-level esbuild calls decrease from three to one, while the chat call remains.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same script process started three independent splitting-enabled Mermaid builds plus the separate chat build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Build/prepublish waits for completion; watch output becomes usable after the corresponding builds finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and bundle dependency graphs, build embedded diagram CSS/fonts, write entry modules and dependency chunks, and subscribe to source-file events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Common Mermaid dependencies and CSS plugin work previously participated in three independent graphs/output sets; now one combined graph/output set. Chat remains separate. Packaging includes webview-out because .vscodeignore does not exclude output folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Three separate folders stored separate shared/deferred chunks and three watchers triggered fresh builds for each shared-source edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dependency reads and output writes are required for build completion; source subscriptions persist in watch mode.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three entries share the Mermaid/shared dependency graph, including layout/ZenUML modules and dynamic icon-pack imports. Source edits anywhere in the shared previewSrcDir previously triggered three independent builds of that graph; now they trigger one. Chat has its existing separate run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Previously four concurrent run calls (chat plus three Mermaid contexts); now two. The esbuild service is shared rather than one service subprocess per run. Previously three independent watchers subscribed to the same previewSrcDir; now one combined-build watcher does. Existing overlapping rebuild behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The common runner intentionally retains no esbuild context across watch rebuilds, so each debounced event is a fresh bundling operation. Multi-entry splitting now shares emitted dependency chunks within one build rather than duplicating them between three output folders. Output-directory cleanup is absent before and after; stale files from earlier builds are not a newly introduced cleanup mechanism.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed run cardinality, identical imported common modules, common watch roots, fresh-build behavior, and product/prepublish callers are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No builds were executed and emitted outputs were unavailable; exact bytes, file counts, build durations, and peak memory were not independently measured. PR-stated measurements were not treated as proof.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression established. This removes concrete repeated bundling/output work; the additional standalone editor build's introducing commit was resolved with blame and the fix was recorded internally. Chat build semantics and options remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update a Markdown preview containing Mermaid diagrams, including icon-bearing or alternate-layout diagrams
Scenarios.CriticalPath: documentRenderer emits one module script for the Mermaid contribution. Its entry and static imports must load before init initializes Mermaid, awaits addon registration, and renders diagrams. First use of deferred diagram/icon code can wait for additional chunk loads. Subsequent content/theme events render again in the existing context.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the entry and imported chunks through webview URLs; the service worker forwards resource requests to the host and receives streamed responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One contributed entry plus unique reachable emitted chunk URLs per module context, with deferred requests for actually used loaders; warm module imports avoid reissuance within that context. New contexts may revalidate cached URLs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same module-script path and split/lazy loading existed under markdown-preview-out/index.js; only emitted grouping and URLs change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required static chunks block entry evaluation; deferred chunks block first rendering that needs them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve resource containment using provider realpath where supported, then readFileStream with an optional ETag; remote providers may cross remote I/O boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per issued unique-resource request: containment/provider work and a conditional stream read; warm revalidation can return NotModified without retransferring the body. Unusual symlink-root resolution can inspect several roots, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical host loader served the preview's old entry/chunk paths, with extension-level resource roots and the same caching and limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for each requested resource response, including cold module loads and warm validation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One entry per preview context, unique reachable static chunk URLs plus distinct lazy chunks actually requested by diagram types/icon packs, and N diagram render operations per update. Module loads are not N independent full-bundle loads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The renderer schedules existing per-diagram promises and awaits Promise.all; the internal Mermaid scheduling is dependency-owned and unchanged. Resource requests use the existing 32-active-host-response-body semaphore on Electron; other platforms keep existing browser/provider scheduling. No new per-diagram boundary loop or concurrency control change appears.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser module identity deduplicates successful imports within a context; icon loaders remain dynamic imports. The existing service worker caches GET responses by request URL and ETag, revalidating warm requests with the host. Renaming folders changes initial URL keys but does not change ongoing invalidation or negative-cache behavior. Render cancellation and state retention remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for execution path and unchanged scheduling/cache ownership; insufficient evidence for a newly expensive runtime graph.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Generated bundle graphs were unavailable, so the exact change in chunk/request counts and timings cannot be established statically. Source imports, lazy loaders, render frequency, and boundary implementations are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression. Combining build entry points does not itself establish eager loading of the other entries or per-diagram network/I/O fan-out; the source lazy-import functions and splitting option remain intact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a notebook and render/update Markdown cells containing Mermaid diagrams
Scenarios.CriticalPath: webviewPreloads caches Renderer.load(), waits for kernel preloads, imports the base Markdown renderer, and loads its extending Mermaid renderer. Mermaid activation awaits getRenderer and addon registration before installing the Markdown-It hook. Cell rendering then performs the existing Mermaid parsing/rendering work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dynamic module import loads the extending renderer entry and its static/deferred chunks through the webview resource bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached entry import/activation per Mermaid Renderer instance plus unique reachable chunk URLs; subsequent cells share that renderer/module state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached activation imported notebook-out/index.js and split sibling chunks; the diff substitutes webview-out/notebook.js.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial renderer loading lies on base Markdown renderer activation; deferred chunks delay first diagrams needing those implementations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/conditionally stream requested modules from the extension filesystem, possibly via a remote provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing loader invocation per issued resource request, with module/ETag deduplication as above; root list cardinality is unchanged, with a substituted directory URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same host path served the old notebook output directory, already derived from the renderer entrypoint's dirname.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resource containment and response delivery precede module evaluation; no directory enumeration is added by broadening the named output folder.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Mermaid renderer activation per notebook webview, not per Markdown cell. Resource requests scale with unique entry/static/deferred chunk URLs; rendering work scales with diagram count across rendered cells and subsequent updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dependent renderer activation uses Promise.all but each Renderer.load() joins its own cached promise. Existing per-diagram render promises remain unchanged; host resource response bodies are limited to 32 on Electron, with existing scheduling elsewhere. There is no renderer reload per cell introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Renderer._loadPromise coalesces concurrent activation requests and retains both success and rejection. Browser module imports and service-worker GET/ETag caches handle loaded chunks. Lazy icon imports remain lazy. Moving entrypoint.path changes its root directory to webview-out, and backLayerWebView derives its allowed root from dirname(entrypoint.path), keeping sibling chunks accessible.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cached activation, derived resource root, source entry/addon/render paths, and common resource loader are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact emitted chunk count and runtime timings are unavailable. The number of diagrams/cells affects existing rendering cost, not proven newly added boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression. The URL/root substitution preserves sibling-chunk loading and cached renderer activation; a larger available directory does not cause loading all three entries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open/reuse Mermaid embedded editors in the Markdown editor, then edit content or change theme/settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host resolves a provider descriptor, constructs a frame with the returned inline HTML/base URI, and loads its module script. Guest main awaits addon registration and WebEditorClient.connect before rendering and reporting height. Content/theme changes invoke the existing abort-and-render path; settings changes invalidate provider results using the existing listener.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve descriptors across the webview/extension bridge and connect the guest to its parent WebEditorHost, exchanging content and size messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bridge requests follow the external frame/provider consumer; expensive provider resolution is shared per provider/document/language key. Guest connect occurs per newly created runtime and content/size messages follow existing edits and changed-height suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider supplied the same inline HTML shape and runtime-key policy, with markdown-editor-out as its base and index.js as the script.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Descriptor availability and guest connection precede first diagram rendering; content messages trigger subsequent unchanged rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load markdown-editor.js and reachable chunks through the existing webview resource bridge and conditional filesystem stream loader.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One entry plus unique requested static/deferred chunks per actual module context, with successful module deduplication and warm ETag responses. No descriptor-HTML filesystem read occurs because content.html is supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent script/chunk requests used markdown-editor-out/index.js and its sibling chunks. Local resource roots already included the extension URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial script/import delivery precedes guest initialization; lazy chunk delivery delays only diagrams using them.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Descriptor resolution is coalesced by provider ID/document URI/language, so identical Mermaid blocks in one document do not each require a new provider resolve. Guest module evaluation scales with actually created/reused frame contexts, not raw blocks alone. Chunk requests scale with unique loaded module URLs per context and requested lazy implementations; runtime reuse remains keyed by HTML-derived runtimeKey.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Descriptor requests for the same key join one promise. Actual frame-pool policy resides in @vscode/markdown-editor and is not available for further inspection; the changed code neither adds a frame nor changes reuse ownership. Different frames keep independent module/renderer state; the existing Electron host resource limiter is 32 active bodies.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: markdownEditorProvider's promise map shares successful/in-flight descriptors and removes failed/empty results; its existing invalidation clears resolved state. Mermaid supplies inline HTML, so the content.uri readFile branch is not taken. Frame reuse is governed by the external markdown-editor package using the unchanged runtime-key contract. Chunk GET/ETag caches and browser module caches remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for descriptor coalescing, unchanged runtime-key reuse contract, inline-HTML path, connection/render sequencing, and resource boundaries; external pool cardinality remains unknown rather than assumed per block.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact emitted graph and external frame-pool size/reuse limits are unavailable. The changed browser test serves a non-splitting in-memory bundle and therefore does not independently establish production chunk counts or load performance.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression. The changed base URI/script name does not add provider work, guest/frame allocation, eager addon imports, or a content/theme rendering loop. Browser-test route adjustment only matches the renamed script and leaves its existing build/browser operations unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass over the entire nine-file inventory and every diff page. Traced build/watch/prepublish and preview, notebook, and embedded-editor loading paths, including shared resource caches, remote/filesystem boundaries, activation/descriptor coalescing, and actual concurrency limits. No actionable diff-introduced performance regressions met the confidence standard. Recorded a concrete duplicate-build regression fix with base-line blame provenance for internal learning. Static review only; emitted bundle graphs, profiling results, and external frame-pool implementation were unavailable.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
